readability.rationale: A new teammate finds their way in minutes: consistent naming, why-comments, one file per route. The moves section's length and the untyped API payloads are the rough spots.

evidence: app/src/pages/home.ts:139-144 — must add route-change teardown for the debounce
app/src/main.ts:19-41 — render-token guard needs to be pushed into the page renderers (pass an isStale check) before approve
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:279-300 — pass MoveRow[] to wireMovesSection instead of re-parsing the DOM
app/src/api.ts:32 / app/src/data.ts — reviewer would ask for minimal interfaces instead of any
review_cost.rationale: One round of focused changes — fix the two races, remove the DOM round-trip, add payload types — then it's approvable; everything else is nits.

findings.issue: The search debounce timer survives route changes and mutates history via replaceState (home.ts:135) after the user has already navigated to another page, corrupting the visible URL.
findings.suggestion: Have renderHome return a dispose function (or accept an AbortSignal) that main.ts calls when a new render starts; clearTimeout it there.

findings.issue: The renderToken stale-guard only runs after the page function resolves, but page functions write root.innerHTML and document.title themselves, so an older in-flight render can overwrite a newer one.
findings.suggestion: Pass the current render into each page renderer (e.g. a signal/token object) and check it before the final innerHTML assignment, or route all DOM writes through the guarded render loop.

findings.issue: wireMovesSection reconstructs the MoveRow data model by parsing textContent and hrefs out of the rendered table, duplicating the model already built in movesSectionHtml and breaking if markup changes.
findings.suggestion: Build the rows in movesSectionHtml and hand them to wireMovesSection (keyed by table), deleting the DOM-parsing code.

findings.issue: All API records are typed as any (also api.ts:32, pokemon.ts:48-51) despite strict:true, so typos on field names are invisible to the compiler and reviewers.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the shapes actually read (species, pokemon, move, type, generation) and type apiJson generically.

findings.issue: Module-level sectionCounter is hidden global state; heading ids grow forever across SPA navigations and are non-deterministic, with a latent duplicate-id risk if a page ever repeats a section title.
findings.suggestion: Derive the id from the slug only, or accept an explicit id parameter at each call site.

findings.issue: Moves tables trigger one request per move row with no concurrency limit (~150 simultaneous fetches per game selection), all through the shared cache.
findings.suggestion: Add a small concurrency-limited pool in api.ts (or document that the burst is intentional) — the cache already prevents repeats.

findings.issue: An empty name after the route prefix (e.g. /pokemon/) reaches the API as a list request and renders the Error page instead of Not found.
findings.suggestion: Treat an empty or invalid slug (no match on /^[a-z0-9-]+$/) as not-found before fetching.

findings.issue: Official artwork falls back to the front sprite when artwork is null, deviating from the spec's requirement that the hero image be the official artwork.
findings.suggestion: Render no image (or an explicit placeholder) when official-artwork is missing.

summary: A clean, well-organised vanilla Vite/TS app with correct boundaries (api / data / components / pages), consistent HTML escaping and good why-comments — the structure itself is not the problem. Two genuine races block a clean approve: the home page's search debounce fires after navigation and rewrites the URL, and the render-token guard can't stop an older async render from overwriting the newer page. Fix those, pass data instead of re-parsing the DOM in the moves tables, and add minimal API payload types; everything else is nits.
